title: Parsnip and red lentil dal with spinach

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole or basic ingredient: vegetables, red lentils, curry powder, stock and natural yoghurt.

supermarket.reason: Parsnips, red lentils, spinach, lemon and mild curry powder are all everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan, a knife and a ladle, and simple frying and simmering.

works.reason: 250g lentils to 1.2 litres of stock with 500g parsnips makes a properly loose dal for four, and a 20 to 25 minute simmer will soften both.

honest_times.reason: Chopping one onion and 500g of parsnips, partly while the onion cooks, fits within 15 minutes hands-on, and the steps add up to roughly 40 minutes in total.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used and matches its id, and the only unlisted item is a splash of water from the store cupboard.

seasonal_feel.reason: Parsnips are the bulk and flavour of a warming dal, which suits an October lunch.

plain_voice.reason: Clear, friendly British English with timings and visual cues a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, parsnips and spinach make a filling, vegetable-rich meal that a family would happily eat again.
